gaps.fact: Columbia Gorge as the third AVA shared by Washington and Oregon: the oregon and washington records teach it (exam, traps), but no chapter names it and no question asks it; c-p6pp51i9 names it only in its explanation.

The Columbia, Yakima and Snake rivers as the water source for irrigation: only the columbia-valley article names them (terroir, water); the chapters say irrigation and no question asks where the water comes from.

Oregon's traditional method sparkling wine: the willamette-valley article and the oregon record teach it (Brut; Argyle in Dundee from 1987), but neither chapter mentions sparkling wine in Oregon and no question asks it.

Domaine Serene, Erath and Ponzi in the Willamette, and Quilceda Creek, L'Ecole No. 41 and Leonetti in Washington, stand only in the two articles' producer lists; no chapter names them and no question of either bank asks any of the six.

The Court's two Northwest pairings, Willamette Pinot Noir with salmon or butternut squash and Washington Cabernet Sauvignon or Merlot with beef or lamb: only the article wine notes give them (butternut squash nowhere); i-akpr1zr7 asks Pinot Noir with salmon without naming Oregon.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 61 (United States, of which 13 are the Northwest: Oregon 6, Washington 7) and Village 33 (Pacific NW, NY & Canada, of which 20 are the Northwest: Oregon 10, Washington 8, Idaho 2), 94 in all, 33 of them this subject's; three more Northwest stems sit in Producers & Icons and Terroir: Climate & Soil (i-13lwy9ne, i-jodhbrgx, c-57evzatn). The most thoroughly drilled of the six North American subjects: the rain shadow, irrigation, the Missoula Floods and own roots, Jory, Willakenzie and Laurelwood, the Willamette sub-AVAs down to Ribbon Ridge inside the Chehalem Mountains, the Horse Heaven Hills and Red Mountain, and Oregon's 90 and 95 per cent rules all have questions. The gaps are the Columbia Gorge, the three rivers, Oregon sparkling wine, six of the Court's producers and the two pairings. No error found: Eyrie 1965 and the Dundee Hills 1966, HillCrest 1961 as the first modern Oregon vineyard, Yakima Valley 1983 before Columbia Valley 1984, the Rocks District on the Oregon side of the Walla Walla Valley, and Oregon's exempt group at 75 per cent all hold. One search spent, on Oregon labelling since 8.2023: it found only the 2019 measures (the conjunctive Willamette Valley rule the oregon record already carries, and a power for the commission to raise the Willamette varietal floor towards 100 per cent from 2030), with no rule adopted since the guide confirmed. The second search, on boundary changes to the AVAs the Court names since 8.2023, found none: the new AVAs of the period, Beverly (2024) and Columbia Hills (2026), are nested inside the Columbia Valley without moving its line, and the washington record already carries both. So courtUpdates is empty.
